findings.description: A finalized poll with durable CLOSED barriers prevented repository startup if the wall clock moved back before its original deadline: its saved result was classified as premature.
findings.fix: Recovery now requires a successful read-only replay of every existing CLOSED barrier and strict validation of the saved result before restoring that final. Open journals are never sealed to justify a premature result.
regressions: Fresh-owner restart inside the original minute and before its start preserves the exact final
Known and new tokens remain closed
Tampered saved results are rejected repeatedly without overwrite
Checksummed premature results remain rejected and do not manufacture CLOSED

findings.description: Files already rejected unsafe Create years conservatively; Create, WAL configuration, and persisted-definition validation now share the exact signed-64-bit UnixNano round-trip invariant for both endpoints.
findings.fix: Reject timestamps that do not round trip through time.Unix(0, t.UnixNano()), including a valid start whose one-minute end overflows; permit both valid boundary windows.
regressions: Minimum and maximum signed-64-bit nanosecond boundaries
One nanosecond outside either boundary and year 3000
No journal or preparation files for invalid Create
Real WAL admission, replay, and recovery at both boundaries

limitations: Race and filesystem tests do not prove power-loss durability or throughput.
Existing guarantees still depend on one owned local disk; disk loss requires separate replication.
A context cannot interrupt an in-progress filesystem sync; Close may wait for that syscall.
No load tests, browser tests, commits, pushes, or production configuration changes were performed by this agent.
